title: World AIDS Day: How Sex Positivity Saved Lives
description: Join the filmmakers and Annie Sprinkle for an evening of film clips and conversation exploring how Robin Byrd’s sex-positive public-access show became a platform for safer-sex advocacy during the AIDS crisis. Commemorate World AIDS Day at The Broad with a behind-the-scenes look at the HBO documentary Bang My Box: The Robin Byrd Story . Before the internet, late-night New York TV icon Robin Byrd used her boundary-pushing public access show to champion sex-positivity and free speech. Across roughly 600 episodes, which she is now working to archive, the accidental activist built a devoted following that by the early 1980s included many gay men, just as a mysterious disease with no known treatment began to devastate their community. description: The Wende Museum presents Seven Sisters Productions in a concert of two premieres about space exploration. The concert is part of the program series for the exhibition Competing Cosmologies: Interpreting the Sky . Silver Mirror is a new work by composer Sergey Nesterov and librettist Alan Olejniczak. Seven Sisters Productions commissioned it for the exhibition. Written for soprano, piano, contrabass, and clarinet, it tells the story of the human space race from the moon’s point of view. The moon first describes its role as watcher and guardian of the earth. Over four movements, it then recalls Sputnik, Apollo 11, the Voyager probes, and the Challenger shuttle. description: On December 12, 2026, The Broad will open a new ground-floor gallery in space that previously held art storage, bringing more of its collection into public view ahead of its 2028 expansion . The gallery debuts with On View , a free exhibition of photography from the Broad collection. Marking the 200th anniversary of the first photograph, On View brings together significant works by artists Gregory Crewdson , Andreas Gursky , Sharon Lockhart , Paul Pfeiffer , Thomas Struth , and Jeff Wall . Organized by Ed Schad, Curator and Publications Manager at The Broad, the exhibition centers on spectatorship, being viewed and being seen, exploring how images are constructed and what truths they offer about the world around us. The new gallery is a sneak peek at the museum's next chapter.

description: Dig into an imagined past with artist Vita Kari, uncovering artifacts that place Deaf and hard-of-hearing experiences at the center of history. Unearthed is a one-day interactive workshop and durational performance by Vita Kari . Participants uncover fabricated listening devices and archival fragments from an imagined past where (d)/Deaf and Hard of Hearing people were always visible. After opening secret compartments embedded in handmade faux rock to reveal the artifacts, visitors receive a thermal-printed field report of their discovery. This take-home record extends the exhibition’s questions of history and memory through the lenses of hearing, accessibility, and disability. title: Ghost Agency: Smooth Criminal
description: Ghost Agency: Smooth Criminal March 1, 2027 – March 31, 2028 Hearth Gallery -18th Street Arts Center Smooth Criminal reimagines public sculpture for an era shaped by digital networks, surveillance, and questions of personal agency. title: Music/Words LA: Curated by Inna Faliks
description: Music/Words LA closes its second season at the Wende with the US premiere of Janáček’s sonata for violin and piano in its early, unpublished version. Czech violinist Pavel Šporcl makes a rare Los Angeles appearance with pianist Inna Faliks in an all-Czech program of 20th-century music that marks the release of their recording on the Pentatone label. Works by Martinů, Dvořák, Suk, Bodorová, and Gideon Klein complete the program, in dialogue with Czech poems read by a poet to be announced. Founded by Faliks in New York, Music/Words is a platform for artists working where music and text meet. This Los Angeles residency at the Wende builds each program around close listening and live collaboration. title: “New Voices” opening reception
description: @ New Voices: THE 2026 ELAC Juried Student Art Exhibition by Monica Orozco. Join us for the opening reception of New Voices: The 2027 District Wide Student Art Biennial . The exhibition showcases student artworks produced across numerous instructional departments, representing all nine campuses of the Los Angeles Community College District (LACCD). It features ceramics, drawing, painting, photography, sculpture, theater and costume design, and mixed media works created during the Spring 2025 and Fall 2026 semesters. The exhibition is organized by the Vincent Price Art Museum and is juried by and curated by Jheanelle Brown. Free and open to the public.
